learningObjective: Compare MinMax, Percentile, and KL-divergence calibration for PTQ activation scales.

canonicalClaims.claim: MinMax calibration sets the quantization threshold to the observed absmax; it is outlier-sensitive. Percentile calibration clips at a high percentile (e.g., 99.9%) to reduce outlier influence. KL calibration searches for the threshold minimizing KL divergence between FP and quantized distributions (TensorRT default).
conditions: Calibration set is representative of inference-time activations.
Quantization scheme is per-tensor symmetric (typical case).
nonImplications: Does not imply KL always outperforms MinMax on all workloads.
Does not imply percentile has a fixed threshold; 99%, 99.9%, 99.99% are tunable.

misconceptions.claim: MinMax is always the most accurate calibration because it never clips any activation.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Not clipping ≠ most accurate; outlier-dominated ranges waste INT8 levels and lose resolution on the bulk distribution.

misconceptions.claim: KL-divergence calibration only works for continuous distributions and cannot be applied to INT8.
misconceptions.whyWrong: KL calibration operates on histograms mapped to discrete INT8 bins; this is precisely how TensorRT implements it.

misconceptions.claim: Percentile calibration always uses the 99% threshold across frameworks.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The percentile is a tunable parameter; 99%, 99.9%, 99.99% are all common depending on outlier prevalence.

misconceptions.claim: Calibration methods only affect activation scales, not weight scales.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The same calibration principles apply to weight scaling; in practice weights use per-channel absmax, but the general framework is shared.

implementationFacts: TensorRT: `IEntropyCalibrator2` is the default INT8 calibrator using a KL-divergence-based algorithm on activation histograms.
PyTorch: `HistogramObserver` supports MinMax and various percentile / entropy variants.
performanceScenarios: For LayerNorm activations with heavy tails, percentile-99.9 typically outperforms MinMax by 2-5% in INT8 accuracy.
For post-softmax activations (bounded [0,1]), MinMax and percentile agree; KL adds no benefit.
